sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the western half of Ocean Park, the 1890 resort settlement that is today the northern part of Bradley Beach. It is bounded on the west by the New York and Long Branch Railroad (its tracks lie just beyond the sheet edge, as a marginal note says), on the east by Fletcher Avenue, on the north by the edge of the sheet just above Newark Avenue and on the south by the blocks below Cook Avenue. South Main Street runs straight down the left third of the sheet; Hammond Avenue crosses the middle, and Newark Avenue, Park Place, Ocean Park Avenue, McCabe Avenue and Cook Avenue cross from west to east. The blocks east of Main Street are laid out in long rows of narrow numbered lots, most of them still empty, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a few stables and sheds, a bakery with its oven on Main Street, an ice house in block 10 and a small paint shop south of Cook Avenue. West of Main Street, between it and the railroad, stand more dwellings and stores in blocks I, II and 12, and at the north-west corner the Ocean Grove Electric Light and Water Works, with its engine house, coal and tool houses and an ice house. The sheet is drawn with north towards the upper left and carries a compass rose in block II. The title cartouche of the Sanborn-Perris Map Co. in the upper right names the place Ocean Park and the date July 1890; the margin gives the series as New Jersey Coast Map nos. 22 and 23. Block 14, south-east of Cook Avenue and Fletcher Avenue, is marked as having no exposure along its southern side.
notes: S. Main is today Main Street (NJ 71).
Fletcher Avenue is today Fletcher Lake Avenue.
Park Place is today Park Place Avenue.
Cook Avenue is today Lareine Avenue.
Ocean Grove Electric Light and Water Works at the north-west corner, west of Main Street.
The scale bar reads 60 ft to an inch while the title cartouche says 50 ft; the fitted scale agrees with 60 ft.
Margin note: New York and Long Branch Railroad tracks beyond the west edge.

Ocean Park, today the north end of Bradley Beach: S. Main (Main Street), Hammond Av, Fletcher Av (Fletcher Lake Avenue), Newark Av, Park Pl (Park Place Avenue), Ocean Park Av, McCabe Av, Cook Av (Lareine Avenue). North to the upper left (about 15 degrees). One part; title cartouche notched out.

sheet-23-1.description: The eastern half of the main map of sheet 23, between Beach Avenue and the ocean front along Ocean Avenue, in Ocean Park, today the north end of Bradley Beach. It runs from the south shore of Fletcher Lake down to McCabe Avenue. East of Beach Avenue the cross streets are Cliff Avenue, Union Avenue, Neptune Avenue and Ocean Park Avenue; Kent Avenue, a narrow 30 ft street, runs north from Cliff Avenue towards the lake and turns north-east towards Ocean Avenue, where the drawing breaks off with a note to see the detached inset. Ocean Avenue, 75 ft wide, runs down the right side of the sheet, with the beach-front blocks 10 and 11 beyond it outlined but left blank; a note in block 10 refers to the detached drawing of the Bradley Beach Hotel. The blocks are laid out in numbered lots with a scattering of two-storey frame dwellings, among them the Cliff Villa on Cliff Avenue, and a few stables; most lots are still vacant, and blocks 4 and 8 are almost empty. A compass rose on the lake shore shows north to the upper left. The street lines are drawn straighter than they lie: Ocean Avenue converges on Beach Avenue southwards much more than on the ground, so this half was georeferenced separately from the western half of the sheet.
notes: Union Avenue is today the east end of Newark Avenue.
Neptune Avenue is today the east end of Park Place Avenue.
Cliff Villa on Cliff Avenue.
Note in block 10: see Bradley Beach Ho. detached map (part 3, not placed).
Hand-picked control at Cliff, Kent, Neptune and McCabe junctions; residuals 1 to 3 m reflect the drawing's distortion.

Printed sheet 23, July 1890, scale 60 ft to an inch. Central Av, Beach Av and Ocean Av between Fletcher Lake and McCabe Av, with Cliff, Union (Newark Avenue) and Neptune (Park Place Avenue) Avs east of Beach Av. Four parts: 1 main map east of Beach Av (drawn with Ocean Av converging on Beach Av about 17 m more than today, so split from the west half at the Beach Av centreline); 2 inset at top left, Ocean Av and Kent Av at Fletcher Lake (continuation of block 2); 3 inset at top centre, Bradley Beach Hotel east of Ocean Av at Neptune Av (not placed); 4 main map west of Beach Av.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Bradley Beach Hotel, block 10 east of Ocean Avenue at Neptune Avenue (drawn at a smaller, unstated scale (streets about 0.55 of their main-map width) with a single junction (Ocean Avenue / Neptune Avenue, today Park Place Avenue); scale and rotation could not be fixed; needs the inset's scale and a second point, e.g. a parcel corner of the hotel lot).

sheet-23-2.description: A small inset in the upper left corner of sheet 23, framed by a heavy border, continuing block 2 of the main map northwards to Fletcher Lake. It shows the west side of Ocean Avenue, drawn 75 ft wide, and the north end of Kent Avenue, which runs diagonally north-east and turns east to meet Ocean Avenue. The block between Kent Avenue and Ocean Avenue holds lots 424 and 425, each with a two-storey frame dwelling; north of Kent Avenue a large lot (lots 426 to 428) reaching to the lake shore carries a large two-and-a-half-storey dwelling, a smaller house, a detached outbuilding and a round ice house. The lake shore is drawn across the top of the inset, with a wooden bridge carrying Ocean Avenue over it. A strip at the bottom marked See Above repeats ground drawn on the main map. The inset has its own north arrow, pointing to the upper left as on the main map, and the sheet number 23 with the words Ocean Park N.J. is printed in its corner.
notes: Placed from a single hand-picked point (Kent Avenue / Ocean Avenue) with the main map's scale and rotation; low confidence.
Kent Avenue now runs straight to Ocean Avenue; on the sheet it turns east at its north end.
Wooden bridge over the lake on the line of Ocean Avenue.

sheet-23-4.description: The western half of the main map of sheet 23, between Central Avenue and Beach Avenue, from Fletcher Lake south to McCabe Avenue, in Ocean Park, today the north end of Bradley Beach. Newark Avenue, Park Place and Ocean Park Avenue cross between the two avenues, and McCabe Avenue runs along the foot of the sheet beside the scale bar. Block 1, between the lake shore and Newark Avenue, holds the main hotels of the settlement at its west end, the Hotel Fletcher with a post office and a second large hotel beside it, and further east three cottages lettered A, B and C, a two-and-a-half-storey dwelling and a few outbuildings. Blocks 5 and 6, south of Newark Avenue, have long rows of numbered lots with several dwellings, among them a house with an annex and the Franklin Villa on Park Place; block 9, between Ocean Park and McCabe Avenues, is laid out in lots but entirely empty. Fletcher Lake, coloured blue, crosses the top of this part, and the blocks beyond Central Avenue to the west are outlined only. The western half of the sheet fits the modern streets closely; it was separated from the eastern half along the centre of Beach Avenue because the two halves are drawn at slightly different angles.
notes: Park Place is today Park Place Avenue.
Hotel Fletcher with post office at Newark Avenue near Central Avenue.
Franklin Villa on Park Place.
Block 9 laid out in lots but unbuilt in 1890.
